primitive.$description: PointSav design system — primitive token layer. Numeric scales (10/20/.../100 for color; 1..13 for spacing; 1..6 for duration) follow an industry-standard stepped-progression convention, so designers recognise the structure regardless of which system they arrive from. Color family names, hex values, spacing values, motion curves, and type scale are PointSav-original. Semantic overrides per tenant brand live in themes/<brand>.json.

orgchart.$description: Org-chart entity-role palette -- 9 entity-role colors x border/bg pair, for hierarchical/structural corporate diagrams.

orange.$description: Principal entity (named individual / equity partner) border

yellow.$description: Fund vehicle / LP / limited partnership border -- dashed pill

magenta.$description: Legacy entity A border -- predecessor structure prior to reorganization

teal.$description: Legacy entity B border -- predecessor asset-holding structure prior to reorganization

utility-4.$description: 16/24 — UI heading, button label, table heading

$value.fontFamily: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif

$value.fontFamily: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif

mono.$description: 15/22.5 — general-purpose monospace: cost codes, work-package/record IDs, command-composer syntax, tabular numeric columns (IBM Plex Mono, variable weight 100-900). Companion to the platform's IBM Plex Sans (see wiki-body); promoted from app-privategit-construction's own self-hosted usage (Version 3 Phase 6) to a durable shared token, 2026-09-16.

viewport.$description: Wiki platform responsive breakpoints — three-tier layout system

compact.$description: ≤ 799px — single-column mobile layout; sidebar collapses to drawer

medium.$description: 800px – 1151px — two-column layout; TOC inline with content

speed-2.$description: Quick — button press, focus ring fade

ring.$description: WCAG 2.2 AAA-conformant focus ring; 3:1 contrast against any tenant background

surface.$description: Dark-mode chromatic-navy surface -- low chroma (0.04-0.05), hue 250/255. Warmer than pure neutral, cooler than blue.

brand-accent.$description: Per-tenant accent pattern -- one CSS custom property set via a `[data-instance]` attribute selector on the document root, applicable to every MediaKit engine (app-mediakit-knowledge, -marketing, -distributions). Only PointSav's own reference value lives here; each adopting tenant's value lives in that tenant's own media-assets repo (e.g. woodfine-media-assets/token-global-color.yaml's woodfine-editorial-accent-{projects,corporate}), layered on top via the same `[data-instance="<tenant>"] { --brand-accent: <value> }` mechanism.

category-tile.$description: 7-color accent palette for home-page category tiles (HOMEPAGE_CATEGORIES). Live in app-mediakit-knowledge server/mod.rs.

theme.$description: PointSav's own default/reference theme — maps semantic roles (interactive-primary, surface-elevated, ink-primary) to primitive references. CORRECTED 2026-07-29: this is the vendor's reference theme, not a multi-tenant fork target. The design system follows a well-established consumption model (.agent/rules/design-tokens.md): an adopting tenant's own brand customization (e.g. Woodfine's) lives in that tenant's own repo (woodfine-media-assets), layered on top via CSS custom-property override at the consuming application, never forked into this shared core repo. This file previously invited an in-repo 'themes/<brand>.json' fork pattern; that pattern is retired.

ink-placeholder.$description: neutral-60 — 5.27:1 vs surface-base (AA). Was neutral-50 (3.33:1, real AA failure — corrected 2026-07-17); shares no value with ink-disabled since disabled text is WCAG-exempt (1.4.3) but placeholder text is not.

border-strong.$description: neutral-50 — 3.33:1 vs surface-base (AA non-text, WCAG 1.4.11). Was neutral-40 (2.18:1, real failure — corrected 2026-07-17; used as the resting-state border on select/input-text/checkbox and the off-state track fill on switch, all real required control boundaries, not decorative). Matches the dark theme's own border-strong, which already used this same neutral-50 step.

orgchart.$description: orgchart.* semantic namespace -- entity-role colors for corporate hierarchy visualization. Parallel to the wiki.* namespace.

corporate-holding.$description: Primary group entity; top-level holding company

investment-vehicle.$description: Investment unit; investor box; capital receiver

broker-dealer.$description: Registered intermediary -- broker-dealer, asset manager, or regulatory intermediary

equity-partner.$description: Named equity partner, individual principal, or operating entity

admin-entity.$description: Administrative entity -- titleco, support company, service vehicle

fund-vehicle.$description: Limited partnership, fund LP, fideicomiso -- always rendered as dashed pill

legacy-corporate.$description: Legacy entity A -- predecessor corporate structure prior to reorganization

legacy-asset.$description: Legacy entity B -- predecessor asset-holding structure prior to reorganization

dark.$description: Dark mode semantic overrides — applied via [data-theme='dark'] on the root element. Maps the same semantic roles as theme.semantic to dark-optimised primitive values. Wiki surfaces verified: contrast targets WCAG 2.2 AA minimum for all text pairs.

surface-base.$description: neutral-90 — wiki page background in dark mode

surface-elevated.$description: neutral-80 — card, panel, sidebar surface in dark mode

surface-subtle.$description: between neutral-80 and neutral-90 — subtle dividers, table rows

surface-inverse.$description: neutral-10 — inverted surface (light chip on dark page)

surface-code.$description: near-black — code block background; darker than page to create depth

ink-primary.$description: neutral-10 — primary text on dark surface; 14.5:1 vs surface-base

ink-disabled.$description: neutral-70 — disabled text on dark surface

ink-on-inverse.$description: neutral-100 — text on light chip within dark page

border-subtle.$description: neutral-70 — hairline borders on dark surface

border-interactive.$description: primary-40 — input border, interactive element outline on dark bg

focus-ring.$description: primary-40 — focus ring; 5.59:1 vs surface-base (AA non-text; corrected 2026-07-15, was mislabeled 3.1:1)

interactive-primary.$description: primary-60 — button fill; 6.66:1 with white text (fixed 2026-07-15: was primary-50 at a hair's-width 4.53:1 pass with a wrong 4.8:1 description; moved to match light theme's own resting value for a real safety margin)

interactive-primary-hover.$description: primary-70 — hover state on dark; 9.22:1 with white text (fixed 2026-07-15: was primary-40, a real AA failure at 2.88:1 — dark mode was lightening on hover instead of darkening, the opposite of light theme's own pattern)

interactive-primary-pressed.$description: primary-80 — pressed state on dark; 12.77:1 with white text (added 2026-07-15: this token had no entry anywhere in this governed source at all — only a hand-added, non-compliant value in the generated CSS at 1.87:1, a severe real AA failure)

interactive-ghost-hover.$description: semi-transparent white — ghost button hover on dark

interactive-ghost-pressed.$description: semi-transparent white — ghost button press on dark

support-critical.$description: critical-30 — error text on dark background (AA)

support-critical-bg.$description: dark critical tint — error banner fill on dark page

support-caution.$description: caution-30 — warning text on dark background

support-caution-bg.$description: dark caution tint — warning banner fill on dark page

support-positive.$description: positive-30 — success text on dark background

wiki-link.$description: primary-30 — wiki hyperlink on dark page; 8.64:1 vs surface-base, 6.41:1 vs surface-elevated (AA on both; corrected 2026-07-17 — the prior primary-40 value only verified against surface-base and failed at 4.15:1 against surface-elevated, the card/panel/sidebar surface this token is also used against in dark mode)

wiki-redlink.$description: critical-30 — wiki red (missing) link on dark page

wiki-code-keyword.$description: caution-30 — syntax highlight keyword on dark code block

wiki-code-string.$description: positive-30 — syntax highlight string literal on dark code block

wiki-code-comment.$description: neutral-50 — syntax highlight comment on dark code block

accessibility.motion_respect: prefers-reduced-motion honored at all interaction layers

wcag-target.$description: WCAG conformance target for this design system

contrast-floor-text.$description: Minimum contrast ratio, body text against its surface

contrast-floor-focus-ring.$description: Minimum contrast ratio, focus ring against its surface

motion-respect.$value: prefers-reduced-motion honored at all interaction layers

page.$description: Shared CSS-print page geometry — legal-agreement and financial-statement sub-domains (WeasyPrint, @page rules). The interactive PDF-binder sub-domain uses its own point-space (see pdf-nav below) since it is generated directly in PDF point coordinates, not CSS @page.

size-letter-width.$description: US Letter width — shared by every Paper CSS-print document

size-letter-height.$description: US Letter height (portrait); financial-report-layout's landscape orientation swaps width/height in its own @page rule

content-width-portrait.$description: 612pt - 2x72pt(1in) margins; running-header rule width on 1in-margin portrait pages

margin-cover-top.$description: Prospectus cover page reduced top margin

margin-wide.$description: Agency-suite uniform margin; also the statutory financial-statement margin (all four sides)

margin-trust-bottom.$description: FIBRA Contrato de Fideicomiso bottom @page margin -- from mx-fibra-trust_V2.css `@page { margin: 1in 1in 0.9in 1in; }` (also `@page toc-page`). Top/right/left of the same rule reuse the existing margin-wide (1in); only the bottom is asymmetric, to seat the `- N -` folio. Value-collides with margin-bind-left (0.9in) but is semantically unrelated (that is subscription's binding-wide SIDE margin).

margin-financial-top.$description: Financial-report-layout V5 @page top margin -- from 'margin:1.05cm 1.1cm 1.2cm 1.1cm'. Four independently-set values; no existing 2-token pair could represent this, hence three new discrete primitives (top/side/bottom) rather than forcing a symmetric shape.

margin-financial-side.$description: Financial-report-layout V5 @page right+left margin (both sides equal) -- from the same @page rule.

margin-financial-bottom.$description: Financial-report-layout V5 @page bottom margin -- from the same @page rule; larger than top to seat the @bottom-center page-number counter.

size-letter-landscape-width.$description: US Letter landscape width (96dpi equivalent: 1056px) -- generic wide-page geometry, previously duplicated ad hoc across several org-chart-print predecessor files as a hardcoded 1056px canvas with no token backing it. Same page, rotated -- pairs with size-letter-landscape-height.

size-letter-landscape-height.$description: US Letter landscape height (96dpi equivalent: 816px). Pairs with size-letter-landscape-width.

print-orphans.$description: CSS orphans value for regulated-document print/PDF output -- string-valued (no DTCG numeric $type applies, matching this file's own counter-family convention). Extracted from a legacy document-viewer print stylesheet that hardcoded this with no token backing it.

print-widows.$description: CSS widows value for regulated-document print/PDF output -- string-valued, pairs with print-orphans.

print-body-min-size.$description: Minimum body-text size for web-to-print document egress (a legal/financial document viewer's print stylesheet, distinct from the letter-agreement/financial-statement print sub-domains above).

print-size-h1.$description: Regulatory print-engine H1 size (legal-agreement/financial-statement @page rules) -- migrated 2026-08-02 from the legacy tokens/global/token-global-print.yaml, alongside print-size-h3/print-size-wordmark/print-header-border below.

print-size-h3.$description: Regulatory print-engine H3 size, pairs with print-size-h1.

rule.$description: Horizontal rule / border weight ladder. The 0.5/0.75/1/1.5pt core ladder is identical across all three legal-agreement families and both financial-statement families — the single strongest shared primitive found across every Paper source. Two families extend it with their own emphasis weight.

hairline.$description: Key-terms table, running-header border, data-table header bottom, financial subtotal top rule (statutory)

light.$description: Fill lines/table enclosure (legal); subtotal top rule (financial-report-layout statement theme)

standard.$description: Form cells, signature line, dividers, hr; financial grand-total top rule

emphasis.$description: Warning box, cover-rule, summary-page border (legal); source financial total rule before the yearend bundle's double-rule upgrade

total-double.$description: Financial-statement-yearend grand-total bottom rule, rendered border-style:double (upgraded from the source docx's single 1.5pt per the bundle's own deliberate refinement)

cover-heavy.$description: FIBRA portada framing rule weight -- from mx-fibra-trust_V2.css `hr.portada-rule { border-top: 2.25pt solid #000; }` (the two heavy rules that frame the cover title block). Sits between the existing ladder's accounting-total (2pt) and accent/total-double (both 3pt) -- a genuinely new intermediate weight.

font.$description: Font stacks across all Paper sub-domains. No shared font family exists across legal/financial/pdf-nav — each sub-domain's register drives its own stack; grouped here as primitives so a family choice is never hand-typed twice.

serif-legal.$description: Subscription-agreement and prospectus body/heading text (byte-identical stack)

sans-fill.$description: Subscription-agreement tier-2 fill zones (accessible completion register)

proforma-sans.$description: Financial-report-layout dashboard theme. CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (V5 canonical spec, Fable design audit): was ['system-ui','sans-serif'] -- system-ui is a silent WeasyPrint no-op, falls back to DejaVu Sans (wide, heavy), never the intended font. Carlito is Calibri-metric; render host needs fonts-crosextra-carlito installed. font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums lining-nums is mandatory on every cell -- Carlito's default figures are proportional and would break column alignment without it.

statement-serif.$description: PROVISIONAL — financial-report-layout's classic statement theme; not yet pinned by the not-yet-implemented proforma engine work

pdf-nav.$description: Interactive PDF-binder — Helvetica core-14 PDF fonts (no embedding required)

color.$description: Ink and surface colors across Paper sub-domains. Legal and statutory-financial share pure black-on-white; the financial-report-layout dashboard theme and the pdf-binder each have their own accent palette.

ink.$description: text-primary — shared by legal agreements and financial-statement-yearend (pure black, no tints, audited-statement look)

placeholder-mark.$description: Legal TBD-highlight mark; pair with mso-highlight:yellow in recipe CSS for Word compatibility

surface-tint.$description: Legal table-header/form-note tint; same value reused by financial-statement header-bg

regulatory-red-herring.$description: BCSC/OSC preliminary-prospectus red-herring notice color — NOT brand-derived, a statutory filing convention. Kept brand-neutral deliberately: this design system ships to other tenants.

financial-gutter.$description: Financial-report-layout line-number gutter (dashboard theme only, JS-injected, absent from print)

financial-row-banner-bg.$description: Financial-report-layout section-banner fill -- the ONLY filled row in the V5 canonical scheme (was #e3edf7 with a separate navy ink; V5 drops both the old saturation and the navy ink, using plain financial-primary ink instead). Corrected 2026-07-29 (V5 canonical spec).

pdf-nav-navy.$description: Interactive PDF-binder — inactive TOC entry text, HOME button fill

pdf-nav-grey-light.$description: Interactive PDF-binder — active-entry highlight fill (same value as legal/financial surface-tint)

placeholder-mark-soft.$description: Shared soft fill-in-sentinel highlight for the mx-fibra-trust and mx-fibra-prospectus families -- 'visible on review, not garish in print' (source CSS comment, both files). A softer amber than the existing placeholder-mark (#ffff00). Do NOT alias to #ffff00 -- a deliberate register choice for Mexican civil-law/securities instruments, not drift.

rule-grey-mid.$description: Shared inter-row/rule grey for the mx-fibra-trust and mx-fibra-prospectus families -- distinct from the financial-report-layout greys (financial-hairline #cccccc, financial-row-total-rule #888888). RESOLVED NAMING COLLISION (2026-07-29): the two families' concurrently-drafted DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE proposals independently minted this identical value under two different names at two different layers (mx-fibra-trust proposed a semantic-layer literal 'table-rule-grey'; mx-fibra-prospectus proposed this primitive-layer name 'rule-grey-mid', per its own oq-3 flagging the collision and recommending single-name/single-layer reconciliation). This primitive-layer name won -- matches how the other shared cross-family value (placeholder-mark-soft, above) already works. Both families' semantic layers reference this one primitive.

financial-cell-divider.$description: Financial-report-layout V5 default cell border-bottom (border:0;border-bottom:1px solid #e3e3e3) -- the faint horizontal-rules-only grid, distinct from the heavier header/subtotal/total structural rules.

org-chart-label-ink.$description: Org-chart edge-label ink -- from the Mexico FIBRA prospectus reference implementation (org-chart-print component).

org-chart-role-green.$description: Org-chart-print role band -- from the Mexico FIBRA prospectus reference (Woodfine ownership chain role, consumer-assigned per document). NOT the same as theme-woodfine.css's --wf-green (#198038, the separate Client A chart family's own role color) -- two different real charts, two different real role-color choices.

org-chart-role-blue.$description: Org-chart-print role band -- Mexico FIBRA reference (securities/debt-instrument role).

org-chart-role-orange.$description: Org-chart-print role band -- Mexico FIBRA reference (trustee-bank role).

org-chart-role-grey-border.$description: Org-chart-print grey role band border -- Mexico FIBRA reference (property/asset-entity role).

org-chart-role-grey-edge.$description: Org-chart-print grey-role SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill -- deliberately darker than role-grey-border (#9CA3AF); a border-matched arrow reads too faint against the page. Do not derive this from the border color for any role -- confirmed only grey needs the split, but model each role's edge-ink as its own slot.

org-chart-role-vehicle.$description: Org-chart-print vehicle/trust role (dashed oval shape) -- Mexico FIBRA reference. Matches theme-woodfine.css's --wf-yellow (corrected 2026-07-30) by coincidence of both tracing to the same org-chart palette family, not a forced alias.

org-chart-role-warm-gray-bg.$description: Org-chart-print role band, tinted treatment -- background fill for the warm-gray role (holding companies / passive entities above the management layer). Generic value (not a tenant brand color) -- re-homed 2026-08-02 from a retired standalone color pillar; pairs with org-chart-role-warm-gray-border.

org-chart-role-warm-gray-border.$description: Org-chart-print role band, tinted treatment -- border for the warm-gray role. Pairs with org-chart-role-warm-gray-bg.

type.$description: Per-family typography composites. Ladders are genuinely distinct by document register, not by regulation (NI 41-101 prescribes no type sizes) — do not force a shared scale across legal families. text-transform/text-align are recipe CSS concerns, not part of the typography composite.

financial-running-header.$description: GCPM running()/element() per-line header typography — financial-statement-yearend (finalized). Reference proportions 14/12/10pt (reference-sample-measured) tuned down to 12/11/9pt for this layout.

currency.$description: Set font-style:italic in recipe CSS — typography composite has no italic-style field in this repo's convention

footer.$description: Rendered italic (Helvetica-Oblique) in the PDF generator

mx-fibra.$description: Mexican FIBRA document register (Prospectus) -- 10.5pt/1.4 Times body, matched to the companion mx-fibra-trust family's body register for house consistency. Distinct from legal-prospectus (10pt/1.35) and legal-subscription (9.5pt/1.28). text-transform/text-align are recipe-CSS concerns, excluded from the composites.

h4.$description: Set font-style:italic in recipe CSS -- this repo's typography composite carries no italic field.

legal-trust.$description: FIBRA Contrato de Fideicomiso type ladder (Trust). Times New Roman throughout (serif-legal). Where the source CSS sets no line-height an element inherits the body's 1.4; those inherited values are recorded explicitly.

body.$description: The family's base register. Cover parties/date reuse this size.

h2-seccion.$description: SECCIÓN / ANTECEDENTES / DECLARACIONES / ANEXOS / FIRMAS heads.

h3-clausula.$description: Cláusula x.y heads, declaración leads, Anexo heads.

proemio-title.$description: The two bold uppercase opening headline lines of the proemio.

sig-cargo.$description: The cargo (title) line under a signatory. Set font-style:italic in recipe CSS.

draft-stamp.$description: The cover draft stamp. Non-italic, plain black.

financial-report.$description: Financial-report-layout V5 canonical type scale (Carlito). Explicit px scale, no rem/px mixture -- h1 17 / h2 13 / h3 11.5 / h4 10.5 / p 10 / table 10.

h1.$description: Document title. Carries string-set:doctitle for the running header.

h2.$description: Statement section heading. 1.5px bottom rule (see rule-table-header-top), no fill.

note.$description: Italic set in recipe CSS -- no italic field in this repo's typography composite convention.

table.$description: font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums lining-nums is mandatory in recipe CSS -- not expressible in this typography composite shape, documented here as a hard requirement.

org-chart-alias.$description: Node defined-term alias zone -- italic set in recipe CSS (no italic field in this composite shape).

table.$description: Table geometry. Two distinct column systems — statutory 3-value-column vs proforma wide multi-period.

num-min-width.$description: Statutory value-column min-width (the one px value in an otherwise pt-based domain — matches the source docx)

pdf-nav.$description: Interactive PDF-binder point-space geometry (612x792pt US Letter, origin bottom-left; PDF point coordinates, not a CSS @page box).

toc-entry-first-y.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 565pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

toc-entry-step.$description: centre-to-centre CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 65pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

toc-entry-width.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 530pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

toc-num-x.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 64pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

toc-title-x.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 82pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

home-width.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 64pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

home-height.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 20pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

home-corner-radius.$description: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (project-jennifer, was 4pt -- never matched shipped code; the original value came from an early draft, not measurement. Verified against 3 production binders (MOU, Agency Agreements, MX Prospectus) + the Client A reference generator.)

toc-child-dash-x.$description: En-dash x-position for a grouped TOC child row -- hangs in the gutter, left of toc-title-x.

toc-child-rect-dy.$description: Offset from the row's y baseline to the highlight/link rect's bottom edge. NOT -25pt -- the reference generator's -25/h:24 band sits entirely below the text baseline (a bug, not copied here); -7pt brackets the baseline correctly.

toc-child-step.$description: Centre-to-centre pitch for a grouped child row -- tighter than a top-level row's toc-entry-step (48pt) so hugging children read as a group.

toc-docparent-to-child-step.$description: Pitch from a doc-parented group header (a clickable document that is itself a parent, e.g. Schedules under a Long-Form Agreement) to its first child -- wider than toc-child-step (26pt) so the parent's own grey highlight box clears the child's text by ~3pt.

toc-docparent-link-dy.$description: A doc-parented header's own /GoTo link rect is narrower than its drawn highlight box (which stays at the standard row height) so it cannot overlap the first child's link rect.

active-marker-size.$description: Filled square, deterministic replacement for a WinAnsi-undefined glyph (U+25BA) that readers previously substituted as .notdef, which happened to render as a filled box in some viewers but is undefined behavior. Drawn as a rectangle instead -- same appearance, reader-independent.

counter.$description: @counter-style glyph rules (string-valued; no DTCG numeric $type applies). Shared by the mx-fibra-trust and mx-fibra-prospectus families -- both families' parenthetical inciso/clause markers reference these rather than each defining their own copy.

org-chart.$description: org-chart-print point-space geometry -- fixed-pixel canvas, no transform:scale() anywhere (see the component's own 'core insight'). From the Mexico FIBRA prospectus reference implementation.

canvas-width.$description: Fixed print-pixel canvas width. Drives the page-margin check: max_side_margin_in ~= (page_width_in - canvas_width_px/96) / 2. Not a universal constant -- a different jurisdiction's chart with a different node count computes its own canvas width and re-checks this relationship.

label-max-width.$description: Edge-label box max width -- tuned to Spanish two/three-line role phrases (e.g. PROPIETARIO BENEFICIARIO) in the reference; English or longer Spanish phrases will wrap differently, re-check per document.

node-width-base.$description: Org-chart node box width, base size. Fixed-pixel print-canvas geometry, same convention as canvas-width/edge-stroke-width above. Extracted from legacy pre-generalization org-chart CSS (nodes.css) that hardcoded this with no token backing it.

node-height-base.$description: Org-chart node box height, base size. Pairs with node-width-base.

node-height-tall.$description: Org-chart node box height, tall variant (more label lines).

node-height-short.$description: Org-chart node box height, short variant (fewer label lines).

node-pill-radius.$description: Border-radius for the pill/vehicle node shape (role-vehicle's dashed-oval treatment).

edge-dash-loose.$description: SVG stroke-dasharray for a loose/standard dashed connector (contractual/referral relationship). String-valued (no DTCG strokeStyle $type used here, matching this file's own convention for non-standard-DTCG values).

edge-dash-tight.$description: SVG stroke-dasharray for a tight dashed connector (flow-through relationship). Pairs with edge-dash-loose.

legal-subscription-agreement.$description: Subscription-agreement family (accredited investor + Family & Friends variants — same recipe, differing schedule variants). Renamed 2026-07-23 from 'legal-agreement' — that name collided with project-documents' own templates/legal-agreement.css, an unrelated Shareholder/Constitutional-agreement family. See paper-legal recipe.json oq-1 (now closed) and this file's constitutional-agreement description below, updated in the same pass.

ordinal-marker.$description: Two-level hanging-indent ordinal system for nested sub-clauses. WeasyPrint 61.1 ignores both the HTML type= attribute and ::marker { content } trailing whitespace (confirmed via direct render test 2026-07-22) — this family uses a counter-reset + ::before + position:absolute technique instead, NOT the .cl1/.cl2/.cl3 span-based mechanism used by legal-agreement.css/commercial-agreement.css (36pt/18pt) or cim.css (22pt/18pt). This is a real, deliberate divergence between families, not drift — see 'Open questions' in the originating DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE draft.

third-level.$value: none — (A)/(B)/(C) sub-markers stay inline text within the nested item, per the source docx's own structure; not a real third list level

continuation-indent.$description: Shares the ordinal system's 20pt indent grid — used by .indent for plain indented paragraphs outside a list (e.g. continuation text that isn't itself a sub-clause).

schedule-instruction.$description: Centered italic gating line for schedule-specific eligibility notices (e.g. Schedule B-1/B-2's "Complete this schedule only if..." line). Existed inline in the original Client-A-specific documents; promoted to the canonical stylesheet alongside form-note (same commit, same additive-only status).

address-block.$description: Set-off, non-justified indented block for regulator contact addresses and similar multi-line inserts inside an otherwise-justified list item. Added 2026-07-22 (commit 572b987) after the source docx samples showed these as their own indented lines, not run-on prose.

schedule-footer-format.$description: Per-schedule page-footer numbering. Single-letter schedules (A/B/C) use the established no-hyphen form; multi-character schedule IDs (B1/B2, Friends & Family only) use a hyphenated form — added 2026-07-22 after confirming the unhyphenated form collided in rendered text with the parent schedule's own numbering (Schedule B's own page 11 and Schedule B1's page 1 both printed "- B11 -").

single-letter.$description: Backed by templates/subscription-form.css's own @page schedule-a/b/c rules — verified present in the canonical file.

multi-character.$description: PROVENANCE CORRECTION (caught by Fable coverage review, 2026-07-23): this rule does NOT currently exist in templates/subscription-form.css — it lives only inline in the Friends & Family HTML's own <style> block. Transcribed from the live HTML, not the canonical CSS mirror. The canonical file arguably should gain these rules — that's a project-documents-side CSS change, out of scope for this token draft.

financial-report-layout.$description: Proforma / projection dashboard register -- landscape, wide multi-period tables. Explicitly a sibling of financial-statement-yearend, not the same register (different page geometry, density, and tone). CORRECTED 2026-07-29 to V5 canonical spec (Fable design audit, project-proforma): Carlito font (was a silent system-ui no-op), horizontal-rules-only theme (no tinted row fills except the section-banner), asymmetric @page margins, explicit px type scale.

hairline-rule.$description: Interior divider rules (not the header/subtotal/total structural rules below).

cell-divider-color.$description: th/td default border-bottom -- the faint horizontal-rules-only cell grid (V5).

total-rule-top.$description: tr.total top rule -- 2px, no fill (V5; was the old 3pt total-double single rule).

ink-gutter.$description: Dashboard theme only -- absent in print/statement theme

row-banner-bg.$description: tr.section-banner -- the ONLY filled row in the V5 scheme (#f2f4f7, was #e3edf7). Ink is ink-primary, not a dedicated navy (V5 drops row-banner-ink).

column-label-width.$description: Wide multi-period table; up to 11 data columns

number-format.$value: Every dollar figure in a proforma or financial-report-layout document is a whole number, truncated (never rounded), toward zero on negatives. Only true portfolio-level aggregate totals rescale to $000s -- per-Unit/per-share figures never rescale, matching the standard '(in thousands, except per share/unit data)' financial-disclosure convention.
number-format.$description: Number-display rule set for proforma/financial-statement output only -- NOT scoped to signable legal instruments (agreements, resolutions, subscription documents; anything rendered under the paper-legal component family / page_legal_instrument). Placed under Paper (document-rendering rules) rather than Writing (prose-governance) -- this governs decimal precision, rounding-vs-truncation, and per-Unit/aggregate scaling, not sentence-level wording; the sibling financial-disclosure prose patterns stay in writing.semantic.pattern.financial-disclosure. Scope narrowed 2026-09-07 (see paper-legal-conventions.numeric-precision-family-wide below for the legal-instrument counterpart) after a real live incident: applying this token's truncate-never-round rule to a Client B Resolution (a constitutional-agreement-family legal instrument) changed a stated per-share price from $0.006263 to $0.006262 in 21 places -- an unaudited edit to an operative legal term, not a formatting change. Two independent dual-model reviews (Fable, Opus) confirmed real drafting precedent: rounding/truncation conventions for legal instruments are always an explicit, per-instrument drafting clause (e.g. SEC rights-offering 'fractional cents' / 'rounding convention' clauses), never a renderer house style.

com.pointsav.paper.base_rule: Truncate, never round -- Rust's built-in {:.N} format specifier rounds, not truncates; adopting this requires a shared truncate-then-format helper, not a find-and-replace of decimal counts. Truncation direction on negatives: toward zero (.trunc()), e.g. -$14,163.69 -> -$14,163, not floor-toward-negative-infinity.

whole-dollar-per-unit-standalone.when: A whole-dollar reference amount (e.g. '$100,000 per Unit') appears on its own -- in prose or a headline, not inside a table.

per-unit-table-figure.when: Per-Unit or per-share figures inside a table whose whole-dollar value is >= $1. Full dollars, never rescaled, even alongside $000s-scaled aggregate columns -- matches the '(in thousands, except per share/unit data)' convention. Corrected 2026-08-09 (twice): an earlier draft's proposed divide-by-1000 rescale was demonstrated live to destroy real precision (a distribution-year and a no-distribution-year both displayed as '0'). Carved out 2026-09-07: this 0-decimal-place rule does NOT apply below $1 -- see sub-dollar-per-unit-precision, which takes precedence for those values.

sub-dollar-per-unit-precision.when: A per-Unit or per-share figure inside a table whose true value is below $1 (abs(value) < 1) -- takes precedence over per-unit-table-figure's flat 0-decimal-place rule for exactly this range. Extend decimal places (truncating, never rounding) until at least 2 significant digits are visible, capped at 8 decimal places. Never render as '$0' -- a sub-dollar per-share/per-unit figure that truncates to zero at a fixed decimal count is precision loss on the one number the row exists to show.

com.pointsav.paper.operator_decision: 2026-08-31, project-proforma -- carve-out confirmed after applying the flat per-unit-table-figure rule literally to real figures (Client B Journal $0.000049/$0.000250, Client A ShareCapital $0.0001) rendered all of them as '$0'. This token formalizes that decision fleet-wide; previously a local, unratified judgment call in tool-direct-hold-engine. Formalized as a DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE 2026-09-07 (project-design, master co-sign: operator, in-session).
com.pointsav.paper.examples: $0.000049 -> $0.000049 (2 sig figs at 6dp); $0.0001 -> $0.0001 (1 sig fig shown at 4dp, extend one more place to reach 2 if the source has more precision, e.g. $0.00010 is not fabricated precision -- use the source value's own precision, capped at maxDecimalPlaces); never collapse to $0.
com.pointsav.paper.scope_note: This token's scope is proforma/financial-report-layout documents only (per the parent token's own $description). Whether the truncate-never-round rule -- and by extension this carve-out -- should also reach signable legal instruments (e.g. a page_legal_instrument-rendered document) is a separate, unresolved scope question, not decided by this carve-out. See paper.number-format.legal-subscription-agreement and related legal-family entries, which currently carry their own independent conventions.

aggregate-total-currency.when: True portfolio-level aggregate totals only -- the only place the $000s rescale applies.

percentage-table.when: Percentages inside tables, e.g. 3.44 -- decimals still exist for ratios/percentages, never for dollar amounts.

type_catalog.type: Per-Unit / per-share figures in a table, value >= $1
Per-Unit / per-share figures in a table, value < $1
type_catalog.in_table: min 2 significant digits, truncated, never rescaled to $0 -- see sub-dollar-per-unit-precision
÷1,000, 0 dp -- only place the $000s rescale applies

type_catalog.standalone: $M at 2 dp, $K at 0 dp (existing codebase convention, kept)

com.pointsav.paper.dropped: An earlier draft proposed extra decimal places for computed-output figures (Development Yield, solved rent rates, NOI, ICR) on first occurrence only. Reconsidered by the operator ('it just gets too confusing') and dropped entirely -- every number, of every type, uses exactly one precision, every time it appears.

paper-legal.$description: Cross-cutting legal-document drafting-CONVENTION taxonomy (project-documents-20260717-consolidated-paper-legal-design-componen) — ONE shared base + 5 per-category variant deltas. This is a reusable CONVENTION register (heading form, numbering, cross-reference grammar), distinct from the concrete per-document-type components (legal-agency-suite, legal-prospectus, legal-subscription-agreement) that already ship real CSS. Most values below are PROVISIONAL placeholders — full CSS/pt values are being delivered incrementally by project-documents (Commercial first, from an initial reference-implementation pilot); do not treat as final until that lands. See paper-legal-conventions below for the qualitative per-variant rules (heading case, 'Section'/'Article' presence, cross-ref capitalization) that have no DTCG numeric/color equivalent.

legal-base.$description: Heading-agnostic shared formatting: Tinos type scale, hanging-ordinal clause ladder (.cl1/.cl2/.cl3), party/recital/signature/fee/schedule tables, draft stamp, page geometry. Only the font family is confirmed by the source request; exact pt sizes, line-heights, and margins are PROVISIONAL pending delivery of the reference implementation.

This description entry is left in place as a pointer for anyone who still remembers the old name.

Overlaps conceptually with the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's own schedule-cover variant (apage...epage named counters, 7-variant MOU/Engagement-Letter family) — flagged for reconciliation with project-documents rather than built as a silent duplicate register.

letter.$description: Numbered paragraph, bold Title-Case run-in if headed, never all caps, usually no 'Section'/'Article' word. Overlaps conceptually with the already-shipped legal-agency-suite component's proposal-letter/mou-engagement-letter variants — flagged for reconciliation with project-documents rather than built as a silent duplicate register.

NOT a Canadian securities instrument, NOT the Tinos MOU family. table-rule-grey.$description: The body-row separator color paired with rule-table-row. References the shared rule-grey-mid primitive (naming collision with mx-fibra-prospectus's identical value resolved 2026-07-29 -- see that primitive's own $description).

toc-hyphens.$description: Without it, long SECCIÓN titles broke mid-word under the body's inherited hyphens:auto. A fix, not an incidental default.

draft-stamp-style.$description: Plain black, non-italic -- a deliberate operator-directed departure from the SOMA precedent.

running-header-body.$description: DELIBERATE: body pages carry no running-header text, a departure from the SOMA precedent. See oq-3 in the originating draft.

mx-fibra-prospectus.$description: Mexican FIBRA offering prospectus (Prospecto de Colocación de CBFIs) -- Spanish, LISR arts. 187-188 / LMV / CNBV-RNV / Indeval. Trust-securitization register, not a share/unit prospectus. Sibling of, and informed by, paper.semantic.prospectus (Canada NI 41-101) but architecturally distinct: Spanish taxonomy, no running header, 0.625in side margins driven by a fixed-width org-chart figure (see org-chart-print cross-ref), 10.5pt/1.4 body register matched to mx-fibra-trust. Source: mx-fibra-prospectus_V2.css (commit 4cd669e).

heading-keep-with-next.$description: Protects the element following a heading from being orphaned onto the next page.

cover-rule.$description: 1.5pt cover rule. Two other rule sites in this family: hr.rule (1pt, rule.standard) and hr.rule-light (0.5pt, rule-grey-mid color).

aviso-border.$description: Distinct from aviso-importante -- a lighter interior notice box, sentence case, not bold, 9.5pt.

signature-one-per-page.$description: One responsible party per page -- eight parties: Fideicomitente, Administrador, Fiduciario, Representante Común, Intermediario Colocador, Agente Estructurador, Auditor Externo, Asesor Legal Independiente.

list-marker-alpha.$description: Present so any clause-style enumeration inherits the register -- unused in the current prospectus body.

org-chart.$description: org-chart-print -- print/PDF-safe corporate-relationship diagram (box-and-arrow, percentage-labeled edges) for WeasyPrint-rendered securities documents. Generalized from the Mexico FIBRA prospectus org chart (project-documents, 2026-07-22/23). Role colors are the Mexico reference implementation's own real values, shipped as this component's defaults -- oq-4 (should project-design ratify one canonical role-color legend across all DHS jurisdictions, or leave it per-document) resolved as: per-document consumer-assigned. A new jurisdiction's chart may override its own role-to-color mapping without needing new tokens; the role-* class names are structural (which role band a node belongs to), not literally locked to these exact hexes. Deliberately distinct from theme-woodfine.css's --wf-* chart palette (a different real chart family, the Client A org-charts, with its own separately-approved role colors) -- confirmed two different real deliverables, not drift, during the 2026-07-30 chart-color reconciliation.

role-blue.$description: Fill+border for the blue role band; also the SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill for blue edges.

role-orange.$description: Fill+border for the orange role band; also the SVG arrowhead/edge-stroke fill for orange edges.

role-warm-gray-bg.$description: Fill for the warm-gray role band (holding companies / passive entities above the management layer). Re-homed 2026-08-02 from a retired standalone color pillar -- see role-warm-gray-border for the paired border color.

role-warm-gray-border.$description: Border for the warm-gray role band. Pairs with role-warm-gray-bg.

print.$description: Web-to-print document-egress physics, extracted 2026-08-02 from a legacy document-viewer print stylesheet that hardcoded these values with no token backing them. Distinct from the letter-agreement/financial-statement print sub-domains in paper.primitive.page -- this is the generic egress policy (orphans/widows/min body size) any Paper-backed web page collapses to when printed.

number-format.$description: Number-formatting conventions — string-valued, no DTCG numeric $type applies (these describe glyphs/rules, not measurements). Shared negative/tabular convention; nil glyph and page-number placement are deliberate per-family choices, not drift, and must not be collapsed to one value.

legal-subscription-agreement.negative: n/a — legal agreements do not carry tabular financial data

agency-suite.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, per-schedule named counters A-E

financial-statement-yearend.currency-mark: single $ on the first data row only, no repeated $ per cell
financial-statement-yearend.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, Notes section only — adopted FROM the legal-agreement family's own convention

financial-report-layout.page-number: bottom-right, standard running counter — deliberately distinct from the yearend bundle's bottom-center Notes-only convention

mx-fibra-trust.negative: n/a -- no accounting-negative convention appears anywhere in the file
mx-fibra-trust.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, single continuous counter -- suppressed on cover-page and toc-page. Same house '- N -' form as legal-agreement/prospectus, but a single continuous counter, not per-schedule named counters.

mx-fibra-prospectus.grouping: comma thousands; currency written 'Ps.' or 'MXN' prefix, never a bare $
mx-fibra-prospectus.nil-glyph: em-dash — (used in Base/% cells with no value)
mx-fibra-prospectus.page-number: "- " counter(page) " -", bottom-center, single continuous counter from the cover; folio suppressed on Portada + Índice

paper-legal-conventions.$description: Per-category heading/numbering/cross-reference lock table for the paper-legal component family (source: project-documents-20260717-consolidated-paper-legal-design-componen §2). String-valued, no DTCG $type applies — these are drafting-convention rules, not measurements. Each cell marked HARD (never varies), DOMINANT (default; strong majority of filed-exhibit evidence), or HOUSE (accepted alternative, operator's call).

commercial-agreement.heading-form: Flat 'N. Title.' — bare number, bold Title Case, terminal period (DOMINANT). NOT all caps. Left-aligned (h2 delta; fixes the orphaned-clause-list defect a centered heading causes).
commercial-agreement.article-word: No — bare number (DOMINANT, Weagree: do not place 'Section' before the number). 'Section N.' = HOUSE alternative.
commercial-agreement.cross-ref-capitalization: Capital for internal refs ('Section 12', 'Section 12(h)'); lowercase for external refs ('section 13.7 of NI 31-103') (DOMINANT).

constitutional-agreement.heading-form: Article line 'ARTICLE N' + ALL-CAPS title, centered (DOMINANT); sub-level 'N.N Title' Title Case (DOMINANT). The two levels are always case-distinct (HARD).
constitutional-agreement.article-word: 'Article' = yes (DOMINANT). 'Section' at the N.N sub-level = HOUSE (Canadian practice: bare '1.1'; US practice: 'Section 1.01'). Include a convenience-construction clause (DOMINANT).

schedule-exhibit.heading-form: 'SCHEDULE A' caps label, centered; internal headings inherit the parent document's own scheme.
schedule-exhibit.article-word: The label itself IS the heading (yes). Pick one term — Schedule, Exhibit, or Annex — and hold it consistent throughout (HARD).
schedule-exhibit.cross-ref-capitalization: Capital, e.g. 'Schedule A' / 'Section 2.1 of Schedule A'.

letter.heading-form: Numbered paragraph; bold Title-Case run-in only if headed; never all caps.
letter.cross-ref-capitalization: Match the cross-reference word to whatever the divisions are actually called (HARD consistency rule): 'Section N' if headed, 'paragraph N' if bare.

preliminary-instrument.heading-form: MOU: numbered/lettered 'A./B.'; LOI: letter-form; term sheet: table/bullets.
preliminary-instrument.cross-ref-capitalization: Same match rule as letter; capital for internal refs.

drafting-rules-family-wide: No orphan subsection (near-hard): never a lone 'N.1' with no 'N.2' — a single-block section stays bare under its heading, with no decimal. [Weagree; Canada Justice Legistics; US House Manual on Drafting Style; Adams/MSCD]

Content-driven mixing is standard: subdivide only where 2+ co-ordinate provisions exist; uniform depth across a document is not required. [filed-exhibit: MDRNA/Canaccord 2009; Aptorum/H.C. Wainwright 2020; placement-agent EX-10.10 CIK 1047153]
Cross-reference address grammar has three depths that coexist: 'Section N' (whole) / 'Section N.N' (subsection) / 'Section N(x)' (lettered clause, cite THROUGH the section).

Internal vs external capitalization: capitalize refs to THIS agreement's own parts (Section/Article/Schedule); lowercase refs to statutes or other instruments (e.g. 'section 13.7 of NI 31-103' — statute title capitalized, pinpoint lowercase). Most commonly inconsistent rule in practice — enforce it.
External-reference disambiguation: always keep the 'of <instrument>' qualifier on an external reference so a same-numbered internal section is not misread.

Left-aligned heading is the orphaned-list fix mechanism: a centered heading empties the left margin, so a following indented clause list floats with nothing above it; left-aligning the heading is what the commercial-agreement h2 delta is doing, and it is intentional, not a stray override.
Roadmap chapeau is acceptable: an unnumbered lead-in paragraph under a subdivided section, cited as the whole section.

Do not formally define 'Section'/'Article' — capitalize without a definition; use a convenience-construction clause instead (e.g. 'references to a Section are to a section of this Agreement; headings for convenience only' — Mitel s.1.2; SEC LPA s.11.05 pattern).
The one HARD rule across the whole family: never two internal cross-reference pointers in different case within the same document.
paper-legal-conventions.numeric-precision-family-wide: HARD rule, added 2026-09-07: every operative numeric term in a paper-legal-family document (a stated price, consideration amount, share count, or any other figure the document resolves/agrees upon) is rendered verbatim-as-stated -- exactly as it appears in the source data, with no rounding, truncation, or rescaling applied by the renderer. This applies across all five paper-legal variants (commercial-agreement, constitutional-agreement, schedule-exhibit, letter, preliminary-instrument) -- an operative figure does not become less operative because the surrounding document uses a different heading style. paper.semantic.financial-report-layout.number-format's truncate-never-round rule (and its sub-dollar-per-unit-precision carve-out) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here; do not apply it to a document rendered under this family. Any rounding or precision convention a specific instrument actually needs is a drafting decision stated IN the document's own text (a 'Rounding Convention' or 'Fractional Cents' clause, per real securities-drafting precedent -- see market-practice-citations below), never a renderer-applied transform. Triggered by a real incident (2026-09-07): a Client B Resolution's stated per-share price ($0.006263) was changed to $0.006262 in 21 places when the financial-report-layout token was applied literally -- caught before commit, not shipped. Confirmed by two independent model reviews (Fable, Opus), both citing real SEC/securities-drafting rounding-clause precedent as the pattern to follow instead of a blanket renderer rule.
market-practice-citations: [FILED-EXHIBIT] StandardAero UA (2026); CST Brands UA (2013) — flat '1. Title.' Title-Case sections.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Ares CRE UA; Baxter Intl UA — 'SECTION' label variants.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Smithfield/Shuanghui merger; Mitel Networks SHA (Ontario); SEC LPA CIK 1403528 — 'ARTICLE' caps + 'N.N'.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] MDRNA/Canaccord; Aptorum/H.C. Wainwright placement agreements — mixed subdivided/bare sections.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Libang Underwriting Agreement EX-1.1 (2024); Placement Agent Agreement EX-10.10 (CIK 1047153, 2009) — flat Section/N.N/(a), not ARTICLE.
[FILED-EXHIBIT] Shareholders Agreement EX-10.19 (CIK 1500866); LP Agreement EX-10.21 (CIK 1403528) — ARTICLE + N.N.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Adams, A Manual of Style for Contract Drafting — all-caps readability defect; internal/external capitalization cue; enumeration requires 2+ units; article = a grouping choice.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Weagree — do not place 'Section' before the number; capitalize internal refs; articles advisable past ~7 sections or multiple topic groups.
[DRAFTING-GUIDE] Canada Justice Legistics; US House Manual on Drafting Style — at-least-two-parallel-units rule; statute references stay lowercase.

paper.$description: Paper pillar — print/document-formatting tokens. Primitive layer: Paper pillar — print/document-formatting primitive layer. Covers three document sub-domains consolidated from real, production-grounded drafts: legal agreements (subscription-agreement, prospectus, agency-suite; source: project-documents), financial statements (statutory year-end + proforma/projection report-layout; source: project-proforma/project-totebox), and interactive PDF-binder navigation (source: project-jennifer's tool-pdf-interactive.py, canonical template). Dimension values use pt/in — this is the vault's first print-native token domain; the DTCG 2025-10 draft's dimension unit set is documented as px/rem only, so pt/in are a deliberate, documented print-domain extension (the print CSS these tokens drive genuinely needs pt/in, not a rem conversion). Semantic layer: Paper pillar — semantic layer. Each document family/sub-domain selects margins, rules, type, and color from paper/primitive.json. Nine families: legal-subscription-agreement, prospectus, mx-fibra-trust, mx-fibra-prospectus, agency-suite, financial-statement-yearend, financial-report-layout, pdf-binder, paper-legal (cross-cutting drafting-convention taxonomy — see paper-legal-conventions below for the non-DTCG qualitative rules it also carries).

table.$description: Wiki-article table geometry — promoted 2026-09-08 from app-mediakit-knowledge/static/tokens.css's --k-table-* CSS custom properties (live, working values — zebra striping, scroll-wrap, never-reflow behavior verified against real Wikipedia table conventions, BRIEF-wiki-infobox-table-tokens.md). Distinct from paper.primitive.table (print/legal document tables — different context, confirmed no overlap) and from writing.primitive.rhythm's prose typography (tables intentionally use a smaller font-size than running prose, matching real Wikipedia convention).

sentence-avg-words.$description: House target sentence length — 15-20 word band

sentence-fact-of-record-max.$description: Ceiling for a definition/compliance/legal claim sentence — a target, not a hard gate

paragraph-line-max.$description: Past this a paragraph usually carries two ideas

heading-density-words.$description: Roughly one heading per 120-140 body words

title.$description: Capitalize the first word plus proper nouns/acronyms/code identifiers only

leading-article.$description: No title, heading, or slug begins with the/a/an

default.$description: Name the actor and the consequence

forward-looking.$description: Not-yet-true capabilities wear their status visibly — the BCSC disclosure posture

credibility.$description: Never borrow a named institution for prestige

standard.$description: Each revision pass sets up a clearly better next pass; revise one altitude per pass, top-down

table.$description: Wiki-article table color roles — promoted 2026-09-08 from app-mediakit-knowledge's live --k-table-border/-head-bg/-head-ink/-stripe CSS custom properties. Light-mode values only in this pass; dark-mode values are real and live in the engine (--k-table-head-bg: #1b2027, --k-table-stripe: #14181d under html[data-theme="dark"]) but not yet ported here — flagged, not silently dropped. See BRIEF-wiki-infobox-table-tokens.md.

border.$description: Close to but deliberately not aliased to primitive.json's color.neutral-30 (#cdd1d8) — kept as the engine's real live value rather than forcing an inexact match

stripe.$description: Live engine value is a runtime color-mix() (55% head-bg / 45% surface), not a flat literal — this is a static approximation of that computed result at the light-theme surface values, not a byte-exact port

register.$description: Ordered formality/tone scale. Each level's $extensions.guide points at the mounted project-editorial register guide (the composition seam — the SCALE is a token here, the prose exemplar stays project-editorial-owned and mounted, never forked). Mount timing: depends on app-privategit-design's DESIGN-BUNDLE renderer for the editorial bundle — confirm before treating these as live-servable, not just structurally correct.

com.pointsav.writing.note: legacy register-specialist.yaml; RIBA/IFC-derived, no dedicated editorial guide yet

Applies to compliance financial documents in the financial-report-layout / proforma-vehicle-layout family (proformas, commission/rebate breakdowns, tax/governance guides addressed to investors). No dedicated editorial guide yet -- see pattern.financial-disclosure below for the four concrete patterns this register governs.

profile.$description: Per-audience specialization of a register — mirrors project-editorial's house profiles (register + audience delta).

com.pointsav.writing.delta: concept-why-how-code-edge structure; one jargon-free accessibility sentence per section
consequence-first lead; what-it-replaces section; no code

lexicon.$description: Generic banned/required-vocabulary STRUCTURE. Ships EMPTY of tenant values — a brand override (e.g. woodfine-media-assets) supplies real terms, the same fork-and-repoint pattern themes/<brand>.json uses for color aliases. Shape: banned entries carry a preferred-replacement $value; alternates and a define-before-use exception ride in $extensions.

banned.$description: One token per retired/undesired term. $value = preferred replacement. Empty generically — populated only by a tenant override.

required.$description: One token per required-vocabulary term. $value = the canonical phrase; $description = its gloss. Empty generically.

thematic-anchor.$description: Named narrative themes a tenant's voice returns to (e.g. a real tenant's own set of anchor words). Empty generically.

disclaimer.$description: Parametrized disclaimer-protocol TEMPLATE shapes. $value = template string with {slot} placeholders; a tenant override binds the slots to real entity/jurisdiction values. Craft governed by the legal register (writing.semantic.register.legal).

securities-forward-looking.$value: {corporate_entity} operates {technology_subsidiary} as {entity_relationship}. This material contains forward-looking statements under {act_citations}. Material risks include {specific_risks}. {corporate_entity} disclaims any obligation to update except as required by law.

com.pointsav.writing.bcsc_posture: planned/intended/may/target language required for any not-yet-true claim

trademark-footer.$value: {marks} are trademarks of {owner_entity}, used in {jurisdictions}. This notice asserts continuous use in commerce regardless of ™/® omission elsewhere. All other trademarks are the property of their respective owners.

privacy-posture.$value: This interface operates on a {telemetry_scope} architecture.

page-title.$description: Cross-property <title> formula — already ratified as foundry-page-title-formula-v1 in the legacy tree, genuinely generic and already cross-brand (PointSav + Woodfine properties). Per-property display names are the tenant override; the formula itself is not.

separator.$description: em dash, one space each side

pattern.$description: Named, reusable prose moves for a specific document family -- narrower than a register (a posture) or a disclaimer template (a slot-fill string). $value is the shape/rule in one sentence; $extensions carries the triggering circumstance and a real verbatim example pulled from a shipped document, not invented copy.

financial-disclosure.$description: Four recurring prose patterns from the vehicle-proforma document family (financial-report-layout / proforma-vehicle-layout), each illustrated with a representative example using illustrative figures (not sourced from any specific shipped document). Cross-referenced from proforma-vehicle-layout's Governance-note and Basis-of-preparation-checklist sections, which describe WHERE these patterns go; this register describes WHAT to write there.

basis-of-preparation.$value: State issuer type, security issued, holdings/carrying basis, cost-recovery mechanism, tax treatment, and structural caveat, in that order, each clause factual and unhedged; omit an inapplicable clause rather than stating its absence, unless a reader would otherwise wonder whether it applies.

com.pointsav.writing.when: The single closing paragraph of a vehicle proforma (see proforma-vehicle-layout's basis-of-preparation variant for placement).
com.pointsav.writing.example: Basis of preparation. Issuer: a representative single-investor holding corporation. Security: Common Shares, wholly held by the single investor; subscription $1,000,000. ... No carried interest, no arranging party, no offering costs. Cost-recovery: the commission rebate reimburses the issuer's own documented costs ($35,000 ...), capped, no gross-up. The issuer pays an illustrative corporate income tax rate on the taxable (non-sheltered) portion of realized ... distributions -- see the applicable tax guide for the return-of-capital/shelter detail ...
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: State an absence only when a reader would otherwise wonder about it (e.g. an investor comparing vehicle variants) -- not a blanket ban on stating absences, and not a blanket requirement either.

form-note-overlay-opening.$value: One paragraph, three moves in order: what the base document assumes; what triggers the alternate scenario and what specifically changes; what stays the same and who the overlay does not apply to.

com.pointsav.writing.when: The opening paragraph of an optional/alternate-scenario section (see proforma-vehicle-layout's form-note-overlay variant for HTML placement).
com.pointsav.writing.example: The base structure above assumes the issuer bears its own documented costs directly, with no separate arranging party as a payee. Where an arranging party brings the deal and needs reimbursement for its own offering-related costs, the registered dealer instead pays a commission rebate to the issuer only ... a comparable single-investor vehicle has no arranging party -- this overlay applies only to the syndicated form.
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: Never make the reader infer the trigger condition from the restated table alone -- state it in prose.

forward-looking-inline-hedge.$value: Name what's uncertain and the reason, in a clause not a sentence, reusing the document-level BCSC footer's planned/intended/may/target vocabulary rather than inventing new hedge language.

com.pointsav.writing.when: Any figure or paragraph presenting a projection, target, or planned outcome, inline -- distinct from the mandatory document-level footer (a Paper-pillar template), which this pattern does not replace.
com.pointsav.writing.example: ...the unrealized change in stated NAV is not taxed until realized (assumption for tax counsel).
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: A parenthetical, not a paragraph -- the full disclosure lives in the document-level footer; this just flags which specific number is an assumption.

fixed-sum-not-conditioned-on-evidence.$value: State the fixed amount, then explicitly disclaim that it is conditioned on submitting or evidencing any specific cost, whenever 'reimbursement' framing could otherwise imply a documentation requirement that doesn't exist.

com.pointsav.writing.when: A fee or payment is a fixed amount rather than a reimbursement of specific, evidenced costs, and the surrounding language could otherwise be read as implying documentation was required.
com.pointsav.writing.example: ...forwards a fixed offering cost fee of $60,000 to the arranging party -- a reimbursement of offering costs, not a commission. This is a fixed sum; it is not conditioned on the arranging party submitting or evidencing any specific costs incurred.
com.pointsav.writing.example_source: Illustrative -- representative pattern, not sourced from a specific document
com.pointsav.writing.codegen_rule: Mandatory, not optional, whenever 'reimbursement' language is used for a fee that is actually a fixed sum -- the reimbursement framing plus no-evidence-required fact together create a real risk of the wrong impression if only one is stated.

writing.$description: Writing pillar — content/voice tokens. Primitive layer: Writing pillar — primitive layer. Objective, measurable craft constants sourced from project-editorial's house-core.md (the shared craft foundation beneath all five register guides). Tenant-agnostic — applies to every register, every profile, every tenant. The register/lexicon/disclaimer rule shapes in writing/semantic.json compose over these; tenant-specific vocabulary and legal-entity values live in a per-brand media-assets override (e.g. woodfine-media-assets), never here. Semantic layer: Writing pillar — semantic layer. Generic, tenant-neutral RULE SHAPES: register scale, house-profile deltas, lexicon structure, disclaimer/trademark/contact templates, page-title formula. Composes over writing/primitive.json (craft) and mounts (never copies) project-editorial's register guides for prose exemplars. Ships with lexicon groups EMPTY of tenant values — a per-brand media-assets override (fork-and-repoint, the same pattern themes/<brand>.json uses for color) supplies real terms. DTCG has no array/list primitive; list-shaped rules are modeled as one token per entry, with structural metadata (alternates, exceptions, scope) carried in a documented $extensions.com.pointsav.writing namespace.
